about: Learn A12, How do governments steer energy? The four instruments with their slider ranges and defaults, a real rule of each kind with its jurisdiction and date, and a reference block written by the test (node _tests/learn/test_a12-policy-instruments.js --write). The model is the Plains Grid's planning LP in assets/learn/components/plainsplan.js, with the fleet in a10-emissions-questions.json and the costs in m06-carbon-in-models.json. Money in 2025 dollars a year.

instruments.label: Carbon price
instruments.pays: Gas plants pay the price on every tonne, to the government.
instruments.side: Every gas MWh costs more, the cleaner plant's too.

instruments.label: Production credit
instruments.unit: $ per MWh of new wind and solar used
instruments.pays: Taxpayers pay the credit on every MWh new wind and solar deliver.
instruments.payer: taxpayers, to new wind and solar
instruments.side: It pays per MWh used, so plants get built past what the grid can take in windy hours.

instruments.label: Investment credit
instruments.unit: share of the capital cost of new wind, solar and batteries
instruments.pays: Taxpayers pay a share of what is built, up front; shown as its annual equivalent over the plant's life.
instruments.side: It rewards capacity, not output: a plant that is often curtailed earns the same credit.

instruments.label: Clean-energy standard
instruments.unit: share of the year's demand met by wind and sun
instruments.pays: Customers are assumed to fund the certificates, at the model's marginal compliance cost; who bears it in the end is not modeled.
instruments.side: Wind and sun that ran anyway earn certificates too.

rules.name: EU Emissions Trading System
rules.text: A cap-and-trade scheme launched in 2005: covered plants, electricity and heat generation among them, surrender one allowance per tonne of CO₂ equivalent.

source.label: European Commission, About the EU Emissions Trading System (page updated 13 May 2026)

rules.name: Clean electricity production credit, tax code section 45Y
rules.text: For wind and solar, Public Law 119-21 (2025) ends it for plants that begin construction after 4 July 2026 and enter service after 31 December 2027.

source.label: IRS, Notice 2025-42, Internal Revenue Bulletin 2025-36, sections 1 and 2.02

rules.name: Clean electricity investment credit, tax code section 48E
rules.text: The same law sets the same end dates for wind and solar plants.

source.label: IRS, Notice 2025-42, Internal Revenue Bulletin 2025-36, sections 1 and 2.02

rules.name: Renewables Portfolio Standard (a renewables-only standard)
rules.text: Senate Bill 100 (2018) raised it to 60% of retail electricity sales by 2030, from eligible renewable plants, such as wind and solar, anywhere in the Western Electricity Coordinating Council's region.

source.label: California Public Utilities Commission, Renewables Portfolio Standard (RPS) Program page

context.text: For scale: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory counted 16 states that had adopted a 100% clean electricity standard, with data through 2023.

source.label: Barbose, U.S. State Renewables Portfolio & Clean Electricity Standards: 2024 Status Update, LBNL (August 2024)
